# Laravel Cloud Provider

Manage Laravel Cloud resources.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    laravel = {
      source  = "laravel/laravel"
      version = "~> 1.0"
    }
  }
}

provider "laravel" {
  # The API token may also be supplied via the LARAVEL_CLOUD_API_TOKEN
  # environment variable, which is preferred over committing it to config.
  # If neither is set, the token saved by `cloud auth` is used.
  # token = "..."

  # base_url defaults to https://cloud.laravel.com/api and rarely needs setting.
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `base_url` (String) Override the Laravel Cloud API base URL. Can also be set via the LARAVEL_CLOUD_BASE_URL environment variable. Defaults to https://cloud.laravel.com/api.
- `max_create_requests_per_minute` (Number) The most requests a minute the provider sends to the routes Laravel Cloud limits to 30 a minute per organization: creating applications, environments, instances, database clusters, snapshots, restores, buckets, caches, WebSocket servers and secrets, and updating instances. Can also be set via the LARAVEL_CLOUD_MAX_CREATE_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE environment variable. Defaults to 25. Set 0 to turn this limit off.
- `max_requests_per_minute` (Number) The most API requests the provider sends a minute. Laravel Cloud allows 120 a minute per organization, shared by every token and every run, and refuses the rest. The provider spaces its requests to stay under this, so a large apply slows down instead of failing. Can also be set via the LARAVEL_CLOUD_MAX_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE environment variable. Defaults to 100. Set 0 to turn pacing off. The budget is per provider process: lower it when several Terraform runs use the same organization at once, since their requests together can still exceed Laravel Cloud's limit.
- `token` (String, Sensitive) Laravel Cloud API token. Can also be set via the LARAVEL_CLOUD_API_TOKEN environment variable. If neither is set, the token saved by the Laravel Cloud CLI (`cloud auth`) in ~/.config/cloud is used.
